question: Obtain the expression for the magnetic field at a point on the axis of a circular current loop of radius $R$ carrying current $I$, at a distance $x$ from its centre. Hence write the expression for the magnetic field at the centre of the loop and explain how the field varies for points far away on the axis.

options.B: By symmetry, transverse components cancel and axial components add, giving $B=\dfrac{\mu_0IR^2}{2(R^2+x^2)^{3/2}}$. At $x=0$, $B_0=\dfrac{\mu_0I}{2R}$. For $x\gg R$, $B\approx\dfrac{\mu_0IR^2}{2x^3}$, so $B\propto\dfrac1{x^3}$.
options.C: $B=\dfrac{\mu_0I}{2(R+x)}$; at the centre $B_0=\dfrac{\mu_0I}{2R}$; far away $B$ remains constant.
